lines.text: Why does the same chlorine gas make different bleach related products when the alkali is heated? Temperature changes which chlorine oxyanion forms, and oxidation numbers reveal what happened to the chlorine.

Cold aqueous sodium hydroxide reacts as C L two plus two N ay O H yields N ay C L plus N ay C L O plus H two O, chlorine changes from zero in C L two to minus one in chloride and plus one in chlorate of I, C L O minus. Hot aqueous sodium hydroxide reacts as three C L two plus six N ay O H yields five N ay C L plus N ay C L O three plus three H two O, chlorine changes from zero to minus one in chloride and plus five in chlorate of V, C L O three minus. In each reaction, chlorine is both oxidised and reduced. Oxidation and reduction of the same element in the same reaction is disproportionation.

Use oxidation numbers rather than product names alone, cold alkali gives plus one, hot alkali gives plus five, and both also give chloride at minus one. The hot equation's five to one product ratio balances the oxidation number changes.

Cold aqueous N ay O H, C L two plus two N ay O H yields N ay C L plus N ay C L O plus H two O. Hot aqueous N ay O H, three C L two plus six N ay O H yields five N ay C L plus N ay C L O three plus three H two O. Chlorine, zero to minus one and plus one, cold, or zero to minus one and plus five, hot. Both are disproportionation, chlorine is oxidised and reduced.
In the hot alkali reaction, identify the chlorine species that is reduced and the one that is oxidised, and state their oxidation numbers.

Cold aqueous sodium hydroxide reacts with chlorine, C L two plus two N ay O H yields N ay C L plus N ay C L O plus H two O. Chlorine is the only element whose oxidation number changes. What must happen to it? It rises in one product and falls in the other It only rises, from zero to plus one It only falls, from zero to minus one It stays at zero in both products ay ay is correct, chlorine goes from zero in C L two to plus one in N ay C L O and to minus one in N ay C L, so it is oxidised and reduced in the same reaction, which is disproportionation. B ignores the chloride product, and with no other element changing there would be nothing to accept the electrons. C ignores the chlorate of I product, so nothing would release the electrons. D is wrong because chlorine is zero only in the element C L two, bonded to sodium at plus one or O at minus two it cannot stay at zero.
Adding chlorine to drinking water kills bacteria. The useful species arise when chlorine reacts with water, so identify them from the equations rather than assuming chlorine gas alone does the job.

Chlorine reacts with water, C L two gas plus H two O liquid is in equilibrium with H C L aqueous plus H O C L aqueous. Hypochlorous acid dissociates, H O C L aqueous is in equilibrium with H plus aqueous plus C L O minus aqueous. The active species H O C L and C L O minus kill bacteria. Chlorine has oxidation number plus one in both, hydrogen is plus one and oxygen minus two in H O C L, while the total charge of C L O minus is minus one. Chloride, chloride, is also formed but is not the active species named for disinfection.

This is another chlorine disproportionation, chlorine starts at zero, then appears at minus one in chloride and plus one in H O C L. The plus one species can also appear as C L O minus through acid dissociation.
C L two plus H two O is in equilibrium with H C L plus H O C L. H O C L is in equilibrium with H plus plus C L O minus. H O C L and C L O minus kill bacteria, chlorine is plus one in both.
Write the two equations that lead from added chlorine to the two active species, then explain why chlorine is plus one in C L O minus.

Chlorine is added to drinking water to kill bacteria. Which species, formed when chlorine reacts with the water, do the killing? H O C L and C L O minus chloride, from the hydrochloric acid formed Dissolved C L two molecules only H plus, from the acids formed ay ay is correct, C L two plus H two O is in equilibrium with H C L plus H O C L and H O C L is in equilibrium with H plus plus C L O minus, so hypochlorous acid and the chlorate of I ion are the active species, with chlorine at plus one in both. B is the common error, chloride is formed, but it is the unreactive ion found in table salt. C is wrong because most added chlorine reacts with the water rather than staying as C L two. D is wrong because the trace of acid formed is not what disinfects. m three.

In one reaction between bromine and warm N ay O H aqueous, thirty point two grams of a product containing sodium, bromine and oxygen is produced. Which mass of N ay O H has reacted?

N ay B R O three is zero point two zero zero moles. The hot alkali ratio N ay O H N ay B R O three is six one, so one point two zero moles N ay O H has mass forty eight point zero grams, option B misses that ratio.

In an experiment, zero point six zero zero moles of chlorine gas, C L two, is reacted with an excess of hot aqueous sodium hydroxide. One of the products is N ay C L O three. Which mass of N ay C L O three is formed?
Three moles of C L two give one mole of N ay C L O three, so zero point two zero zero moles forms, with mass twenty one point three grams. The larger options use an incorrect mole ratio.

H O C L and C L O minus contain chlorine at plus one, because oxygen is minus two. minus one is the oxidation state of chloride, not the disinfecting species.

In the treatment of domestic water supplies, chlorine is added to water to kill bacteria. Some chlorine oxygen minus ions are formed. What is the change in oxidation number of chlorine when forming the chlorine oxygen minus ion from aqueous chlorine?
In C L O minus, chlorine is plus one because oxygen is minus two and the ion has charge minus one, elemental chlorine starts at zero. A change of zero overlooks oxidation.
Chlorine gas is widely used to treat contaminated water. When chlorine is added to water, which chemical species present is responsible for killing bacteria?
C L O minus is an active chlorine species that kills bacteria. chloride is a separate product and is not the active disinfectant.

The hot alkali equation gives six N ay O H five N ay C L. Hence zero point six zero zero moles N ay O H makes zero point five zero zero moles N ay C L, zero point six zero zero moles ignores the five to six ratio.

eleven point four The reactions of chlorine.
In one breath.
Chlorine reacts with aqueous sodium hydroxide to give two products containing chlorine at different oxidation numbers. In water, it produces H O C L and C L O minus, which kill bacteria.
Key ideas.

Disproportionation means oxidation and reduction of the same element in the same reaction. Chlorine in C L two has oxidation number zero. In both reactions with sodium hydroxide, some chlorine becomes chloride at minus one, so it is reduced. The rest becomes a chlorine oxyanion with a positive oxidation number, so it is oxidised.
With cold aqueous sodium hydroxide, the products are sodium chloride, sodium chlorate of I and water.
C L two gas plus two N ay O H aqueous yields N ay C L aqueous plus N ay C L O aqueous plus H two O liquid.

Chlorine is minus one in chloride and plus one in C L O minus. The Roman numeral in chlorate of I tells you that chlorine is at plus one. Thus one chlorine atom in each C L two molecule is reduced and the other is oxidised.
With hot aqueous sodium hydroxide, sodium chlorate of V replaces sodium chlorate of I.
three C L two gas plus six N ay O H aqueous yields five N ay C L aqueous plus N ay C L O three aqueous plus three H two O liquid.

Here chlorine becomes minus one in chloride or plus five in C L O three minus. The coefficients matter, six chlorine atoms enter, five become chloride and one becomes chlorate of V. The change from zero to plus five for one atom balances five changes from zero to minus one.
For water purification, chlorine reacts with water.
C L two gas plus H two O liquid is in equilibrium with H C L aqueous plus H O C L aqueous.
Hypochlorous acid can dissociate.
H O C L aqueous is in equilibrium with H plus aqueous plus C L O minus aqueous.

Both H O C L and C L O minus are active species that kill bacteria. Chlorine is plus one in each, in neutral H O C L, hydrogen contributes plus one and oxygen minus two, in C L O minus, oxygen contributes minus two and the total charge is minus one.
Method.
Identify whether the alkali is cold or hot. Write N ay C L O for cold conditions and N ay C L O three for hot conditions.
Balance chlorine atoms first, then sodium, oxygen and hydrogen. For hot alkali, the ratio is three C L two to six N ay O H to five N ay C L to one N ay C L O three.
Assign oxidation numbers to chlorine in the reactant and each product. State both the increase and decrease when explaining disproportionation.
Worked example.

Explain why chlorine and hot aqueous sodium hydroxide undergo disproportionation. three C L two plus six N ay O H yields five N ay C L plus N ay C L O three plus three H two O. Chlorine starts at zero. It decreases to minus one in N ay C L, so chlorine is reduced. It increases to plus five in N ay C L O three, so chlorine is oxidised. Oxidation and reduction of chlorine occur in the same reaction.
Traps.
Trap, Giving plus five for chlorine in the cold alkali product. Why it's wrong, Cold alkali forms C L O minus, whose chlorine is plus one. Instead, Link plus five to hot alkali and C L O three minus.
Trap, Calling the process oxidation alone. Why it's wrong, Chloride also forms, so some chlorine is reduced. Instead, State both oxidation number changes.
Trap, Naming chloride as the species that kills bacteria. Why it's wrong, The active species are H O C L and C L O minus. Instead, Write the water equilibrium and the acid dissociation.
Exam technique.

For describe, give the conditions, products and balanced equation. For explain, name the oxidation number changes and say why these prove disproportionation. For water purification, give the equation forming H O C L, its dissociation to C L O minus, and identify both as bacteria killing species. In calculations with hot alkali, read the coefficients before finding a mass or amount.
